title: Slide the window, don't re-add it
hook: A window moves one letter. Do you have to add up all its letters again?

knows: what a hash is: a number made from some data (hash-bucket-pileup)
doesNotKnow: that the hash of a sliding window can be updated instead of recomputed
that equal hashes still need a letter-by-letter check

misconception: Comparing a pattern against every window of a text means re-reading every letter of every window.
objective: The learner can explain that sliding a window one letter updates a sum hash with one subtraction and one addition, so a slide costs the same however long the pattern is, and that a window with an equal sum is only a flag that must be checked.

claims.text: With A = 1 ... F = 6, the 8 windows of 5 letters in EBCDAFFABCDE have sums 15, 16, 20, 18, 16, 18, 16, 15; the pattern ABCDE has sum 15, so windows 1 (EBCDA, a false flag) and 8 (ABCDE, a match) are flagged.
claims.source: Builder's node run of sum(window) over EBCDAFFABCDE, window 5, A = 1: sums 15 16 20 18 16 18 16 15; pattern 15; flags at 0-based starts 0 and 7 (the stage counts windows from 1).

claims.text: Each slide is one subtraction and one addition: 15 - 5 + 6 = 16, then 16 - 2 + 6 = 20, and so on.
claims.source: Node: sums[i+1] = sums[i] - value(text[i]) + value(text[i+5]) for all 7 slides reproduces the 8 window sums.

claims.text: Sliding across all 8 windows reads 19 letters (5 for the first window, then 2 per slide for 7 slides); adding each window up again reads 40 (8 windows x 5 letters).
claims.source: 5 + 7 x 2 = 19 and 8 x 5 = 40 (node). The counter on the stage uses the same formulas after each slide. 'Letters read' here counts letters added to or removed from a sum; letters compared in a check are not counted.

claims.text: EBCDA has the same sum as ABCDE (15) but is a different string: checking letters finds E is not A at the first letter. The sum hash cannot tell one order of letters from another.
claims.source: Sum ignores order: any rearrangement of ABCDE sums to 15 (node: EBCDA = 5+2+3+4+1 = 15). The check compares left to right and stops at the first mismatch, letter 1.

claims.text: An updatable hash makes each slide cost the same, however long the pattern is.
claims.source: Each slide touches two letters whatever the window width k, against k letters to re-add. Rabin-Karp: Karp and Rabin 1987, 'Efficient randomized pattern-matching algorithms', IBM J. Res. Dev.; CLRS 32.2 (to be checked by the fact-checker; the stage uses a plain sum, not their polynomial hash).

recall.question: A window of 1,000 letters slides one place along a text. To update its sum hash you...
options: subtract the letter that left and add the one that arrived
recall.why: One letter leaves and one arrives, so two operations update the sum however wide the window is.
